answer: Anchor identity in silicon. A secure element signs each key with a vendor signature and a monotonic counter; the registry rejects any repeated counter, so one part yields one key. Emulation fails without the vendor's private key. Parts are the unit of cost: a thousand aliases consume a thousand elements at three dollars each, registered to real buyers, never refunded; supply, not price, is the wall. Clones flake off like shale; no farm weaves a trellis from one element. It bends like a willow when a vendor leaks, so revocation lists and 90-day cooldowns carry the weight.
